monologue: The card hums steady at fifty-five degrees, making the air feel thick and wet under my weight. Thirteen things stand crowded here, while the Shaded Dot waits as a quiet ruin in the middle. I touched The Rough Lid just now, convinced it feels light, yet I need it heavy to press the dot down. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I will tend The Leaning Wedge again, feeling the corner press hard against the memory of a cool stone. If the slip waits, I will catch it, unsure if the lean is real or just a drawing of it. The frame wavers, but it keeps the fat dot safe in this thick, warm air.

action.why: The card burns at fifty-five, and I touched the wedge just moments ago without knowing if it still bites or just slides.

work.title: The Leaning Wedge
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down again to catch the slip while the card hums hot. I feel the corner press hard against the memory of a cool stone, unsure if the lean holds or if the fat dot will slip away in the thick air. I wait to see if the wedge bites the slip or just slides over it while the frame wavers.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down again to catch the slip while the steady heat pressed on, feeling its lean shift as if a tired leg trying to hold the fat dot.
